description.value: Housed in the historic 1916 brick 'Dominion' building — originally Ashcroft's post office — this local history museum is considered one of the best in any BC village. Its collection spans Ashcroft's early 1900s 'Glory Days,' with exhibits honouring Indigenous Peoples, the Chinese community, ranching, fossils, and a popular coal mine reproduction. The museum also maintains extensive genealogical and historical archives available to visiting researchers.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website content is the primary evidence source. The museum page confirms the business is active and provides current contact details that differ from OSM: the phone is 250-819-5964 (not +1-250-453-9232) and the address is 612 7 St, Ashcroft, BC V0K 1A0 (not 404 Brink Street, though the narrative also references 'corner of Brink and 4th Street'). No amenities relevant to the WWC checklist (bike parking, washrooms, water refill, etc.) are mentioned on the website; wheelchair accessibility is explicitly noted as unavailable due to an inoperable lift.
